title: Conditions & Control Flow
description: Conditional statements control execution pathways based on boolean condition evaluation.

quiz.question: In an if-elif-else block, what happens after the first condition evaluates to True?
options: The block for that condition executes, and all subsequent elif/else blocks are skipped completely.
All remaining elif blocks are evaluated anyway.
quiz.explanation: Once any condition in an if-elif chain evaluates to True, its block executes and the rest of the chain is bypassed.

interviewQuestions.q: 01. How does CPU Branch Prediction optimize if-else conditional execution?
interviewQuestions.a: Modern CPUs use branch predictors to guess which direction a condition (`if` vs `else`) will take before evaluating it, keeping the instruction pipeline full. Mispredictions cause pipeline flushes (10-20 cycle penalty).

interviewQuestions.q: 02. What is the difference between multiple `if` statements vs `if-elif-else` chain?
interviewQuestions.a: Multiple `if` statements evaluate EVERY condition independently regardless of prior results. An `if-elif-else` chain stops evaluating as soon as one condition returns True.

interviewQuestions.q: 03. How does Python 3.10+ Pattern Matching (`match-case`) compare to traditional `if-elif`?
interviewQuestions.a: `match-case` (similar to switch-case in C/Java) provides structural pattern matching for data types, sequences, and dictionary patterns with higher readability and optimization.

interviewQuestions.q: 04. What is Nested Conditions and how to refactor deep nesting using Guard Clauses?
interviewQuestions.a: Deeply nested `if` statements create unreadable "Pyramid of Doom" code. Guard clauses handle error conditions early with `return` or `raise`, flattening the main happy path execution.

interviewQuestions.q: 05. What is the difference between Bitwise AND (&) vs Logical AND (and) in conditional checks?
interviewQuestions.a: `and` evaluates short-circuit boolean logic. `&` evaluates bitwise operations on integer bits or set intersection without short-circuiting, which can trigger AttributeError/IndexError if applied to objects.

interviewQuestions.q: 06. What is Truthy and Falsy coercion in Python conditional statements?
interviewQuestions.a: Python implicitly coerces non-boolean values in `if obj:`: `0`, `0.0`, `""`, `[]`, `{}`, `None`, and `False` evaluate to Falsy. Non-empty objects evaluate to Truthy.

interviewQuestions.q: 07. How to avoid dangling `else` ambiguities in programming languages?
interviewQuestions.a: In languages without mandatory braces (like C/C++), an `else` binds to the nearest preceding `if`. Always use curly braces `{}` in C/Java and proper indentation in Python to prevent bugs.

interviewQuestions.q: 08. How does the Ternary Operator inline conditional assignment work?
interviewQuestions.a: `status = "Adult" if age >= 18 else "Minor"`. It keeps code concise for single assignments but should be avoided if nested multiple times.

interviewQuestions.q: 09. How do logical De Morgan's Laws simplify complex boolean conditions?
interviewQuestions.a: De Morgan's Laws: `not (A and B)` is equivalent to `(not A) or (not B)`. `not (A or B)` is equivalent to `(not A) and (not B)`.

interviewQuestions.q: 10. What is the execution performance cost of dynamic type checks inside hot loops?
interviewQuestions.a: Calling `isinstance()` or `type()` inside loops running millions of times adds overhead. Prefer polymorphism or pre-validating types outside the loop.

interviewQuestions.q: 11. What is the fallback `else` clause in Python `for` and `while` loops?
interviewQuestions.a: An `else` attached to a loop executes ONLY if the loop finishes naturally without encountering a `break` statement.

interviewQuestions.q: 12. What is a Lookup Table / Dispatch Table dictionary alternative to long if-elif chains?
interviewQuestions.a: Instead of 20 `elif` checks, store function references in a dictionary `handlers = {'add': do_add, 'sub': do_sub}` and invoke `handlers[op]()` in O(1) time.

interviewQuestions.q: 13. How does short-circuit evaluation prevent Null Pointer Exceptions in conditionals?
interviewQuestions.a: `if user is not None and user.is_active:` skips checking `.is_active` if `user` is `None`, preventing AttributeError crashes.

interviewQuestions.q: 14. How to perform range checks cleanly in Python vs Java?
interviewQuestions.a: Python supports chained comparisons `if 18 <= age <= 65:`. Java requires explicit AND conjunction `if (age >= 18 && age <= 65)`.

interviewQuestions.q: 15. What is the difference between `pass` and `...` (Ellipsis) in conditional stubs?
interviewQuestions.a: `pass` is a null statement that does nothing. `...` (Ellipsis) is a singleton object often used as a placeholder in unwritten conditional branches or function bodies.

interviewQuestions.q: 16. Why is comparing floating point values with `==` dangerous in conditions?
interviewQuestions.a: Due to IEEE-754 precision errors, `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is False. Always check `abs(a - b) < 1e-9` or `math.isclose(a, b)`.

interviewQuestions.q: 17. What is a Sentinel Value in conditional search loops?
interviewQuestions.a: A special dummy value (like `-1` or `None` or `object()`) used to detect end-of-data or missing search items.

interviewQuestions.q: 18. What is any() and all() built-in conditional aggregators in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `all([a, b, c])` returns True if ALL elements evaluate to True. `any([a, b, c])` returns True if AT LEAST ONE element evaluates to True.

interviewQuestions.q: 19. How to test edge-cases in conditional branching logic during unit testing?
interviewQuestions.a: Achieve 100% Branch Coverage by writing test cases that hit boundary values (e.g. `score = 79`, `score = 80`, `score = 81`) for every decision branch.

interviewQuestions.q: 20. What are production best practices for clean conditional logic?
interviewQuestions.a: Keep conditions positive (`if is_valid` over `if not is_invalid`), extract complex conditions into descriptive boolean variables, and flatten nesting with guard clauses.
